messages:
maria: Quick Q — we need to lock down the embeddings endpoint behavior before the SDK change. Specifically: allowed input types, truncation, batch limits, and how we indicate vector shape in responses. @lina can you confirm current semantics?
ken: Short answer: supports a single string or an array of strings. We treat each array element as an independent item to embed.
ashwin: Also handles bytes/utf8; we normalize to unicode NFKC before tokenizing. Important for emoji and accented chars.
lina: Confirming: POST /v1/embeddings accepts {"model":..., "input": string | [string], optional "truncate": "none|start|end" } by convention. Default truncate="end".
maria: How do we truncate? by tokens or characters? We need deterministic behavior for users.
lina: By tokens using the model's tokenizer. We have a per-model token limit param: model.max_input_tokens. We drop tokens according to truncate policy.
ken: Implementation detail: we currently run tokenizer then clip tokens for each item. So an array with one huge item and 100 tiny items is still limited by per-item token cap, not a global token budget.
ashwin: For batches, what's the limit on number of items per request? SDK needs to enforce.
lina: Current soft limit is 1024 items per request, but we enforce a hard limit at the gateway of 2048 to protect memory. Recommend SDK default to 512 to be conservative.
maria: Is there any global combined token cap for a batch (sum of tokens across items)?
lina: Not enforced today, but we should. Proposal: max_total_tokens_per_request = 131072 (128k tokens). If exceeded, return 413 with JSON: {error:..., code: "batch_token_limit"}.
ken: Good call — avoids OOM. Also note that KV caching isn't involved here.
maria: Output vector length — some users expect a fixed dimension. If we onboard new models with different dims, how do we signal it?
lina: We'll include a metadata field on the response: "vector_length": "1536" (string for compatibility), and each item in "data" is "embedding": [float,...]. So clients can validate length.
ashwin: For backward compatibility: if model X changes vector length in a patch release, do we break users?
lina: We will never change a model's embedding dimension in-place. If a new dimension is needed, we create a new model id (e.g., "embed-compat-v2"). If a customer pins "embed-legacy" they keep the old dim.
maria: What about empty string or null elements in array? Return error or embed as zero vector?
lina: We return a valid embedding for empty string (tokenized empty => vector per model). Null/None elements are invalid — 400 with code "invalid_input_item" and position index.
ken: Example response snippet to include in SDK docs:```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "model": "embed-lite-1536",
  "vector_length": "1536",
  "data": [
    {"index":0, "embedding": [0.0012, -0.0034, ...], "object": "embedding"},
    {"index":1, "embedding": [0.0021, 0.0005, ...], "object": "embedding"}
  ]
}```
maria: Nice. Need to capture error codes: token truncation is silent or do we warn?
lina: Truncation is silent by default. We can add a response header X-Embedding-Truncated: counts or a warning field if any item was truncated, but that would add noise. Proposal: silent truncation unless request sets "warn_on_truncate": true, then return "truncation": [{"index":0, "dropped_tokens":123}, ...].
ashwin: I like warn_on_truncate true as opt-in. Default silent is least surprising.
ken: Do we need to support streaming for embeddings? not applicable today.
ci-bot: Deploy preview for embed-gateway branch is up: https://ci.redwood.internal/1234 — load tests show memory spikes at 600 items * 8k tokens.
maria: Action items: 1) @lina add vector_length field to response docs + example. 2) SDK: clamp default batch size to 512 and expose truncate param. 3) infra: add total token cap enforcement to gateway (proposal 128k). 4) docs: document warn_on_truncate.
lina: I'll open a PR for spec + example and add test cases for empty string, null items, unicode normalization, and warn_on_truncate.
ken: I'll add gateway check for total tokens and return 413 with code.
nashwin: I'll add load test scenarios for mixed-size batches and update the tokenizer normalization test.
maria: Thanks. If no blockers I'll mark this as final for the SDK change set. :thumbsup:
